$comment: Camera framing and motion for the video layer (PHASE 9). A camera move here is a transform over the rendered avatar frames, not a re-generation - it can only ever reframe pixels that already exist. See DECISIONS.md ADR-034.

canvas.$comment: 16:9 because the avatar assets are 1:1 and the remaining width is where subtitles, b-roll, and lower thirds live. fps is never set here - it is inherited from the frame plan, so the video cannot disagree with the lip-sync it carries.

avatar.$comment: source_resolution is ASSET_SPEC section 1. height_fraction leaves headroom: at 0.82 of a 1080 canvas the avatar draws at 886px from a 1024px source, so a push-in of up to 1.156x still samples down. Past that the renderer is inventing detail.

class_ratios.$comment: visual-spec.md section 2, head height as a ratio to close-up (ADR-014). A camera cannot cross a class: pushing a three-quarter pose into close-up framing enlarges a head that was rendered at 0.48 of the close-up size, and every skin and hair detail the close-up assets have is simply absent.

limits.$comment: max_sampling_ratio 1.0 means: never draw a source pixel larger than one output pixel. It is a WARN and not a FAIL because a 1.05 overshoot on one frame of a slow push is not visible, while refusing it outright would make every push-in unusable.

easing.$comment: GSAP easing names (ADR-032). The sampled per-frame values in the plan are what a renderer must use; these names travel with them so a GSAP renderer can reproduce the same curve rather than approximate it.

moves.$comment: Named presets. scale is relative to the avatar's resting size; pan is a fraction of canvas width/height. A narration camera that moves faster than this stops being a camera and becomes an effect.

static.description: no movement - the default, and correct for most narration

slow-push.description: imperceptible push in over the whole clip; adds attention without announcing itself

slow-pull.description: reverse of slow-push; opens the frame as a section closes

settle.description: starts fractionally wide and settles; hides the first-frame cut

drift-left.description: slow lateral drift, for a pointing or presenting pose that needs space on one side
